$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-7-6\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$" :question/worked-solution "Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$

$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 \\ 6 & -7\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

"question-59a82201-03c5-57db-ad1f-7c04fbb98da0" :question/id #uuid "59a82201-03c5-57db-ad1f-7c04fbb98da0" :question/math-academy-id "q-39157" :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}16 & -10 \\ 17 & -10\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above.
Given that $A$ has the complex eigenvalue $\lambda =3-\text{i},$ and that $A=PC{P}^{-1}$ where $C$ is a rotation-scaling matrix, what is the value of 
$\frac{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}?$" :question/worked-solution "Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

Since we are given the eigenvalue $\lambda =3-\text{i},$ we can immediately construct the rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=3-\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -10 \\ 17 & -10\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 3-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13+\text{i} & -10 \\ 17 & -13+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}=0 \\ 17{x}_{1}+(-13+\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix $A-\lambda I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ \frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=10$, we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 13+\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we can construct the matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 13 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}=\frac{{10}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{{13}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\frac{10}{17}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7cbd9e54-5f08-5851-844d-53c1919540be"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-7cbd9e54-5f08-5851-844d-53c1919540be" :answer-field/id #uuid "7cbd9e54-5f08-5851-844d-53c1919540be" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3060d69a-8868-5172-98ad-30a1f7c52b08" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3060d69a-8868-5172-98ad-30a1f7c52b08" "answer-d1e1a656-0f4d-5746-87e0-6a88b18aafd0" "answer-95fee729-2135-5651-b276-0d9f45ed5e6c" "answer-5205fd9c-21af-5e9d-977c-cdc6794be310" "answer-4fac5dc4-ba16-5d80-bb5f-c21a117180c3"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3060d69a-8868-5172-98ad-30a1f7c52b08" :answer/id #uuid "3060d69a-8868-5172-98ad-30a1f7c52b08" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{10}{17}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d1e1a656-0f4d-5746-87e0-6a88b18aafd0" :answer/id #uuid "d1e1a656-0f4d-5746-87e0-6a88b18aafd0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{13}{18}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-95fee729-2135-5651-b276-0d9f45ed5e6c" :answer/id #uuid "95fee729-2135-5651-b276-0d9f45ed5e6c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{14}{17}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5205fd9c-21af-5e9d-977c-cdc6794be310" :answer/id #uuid "5205fd9c-21af-5e9d-977c-cdc6794be310" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{15}{19}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4fac5dc4-ba16-5d80-bb5f-c21a117180c3" :answer/id #uuid "4fac5dc4-ba16-5d80-bb5f-c21a117180c3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{19}{14}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-d6880ebc-9daa-5cd0-b5d7-2100fa039d06" :question/id #uuid "d6880ebc-9daa-5cd0-b5d7-2100fa039d06" :question/math-academy-id "q-99345" :question/problem "$$

Since we are given the eigenvalue $\lambda =3-\text{i},$ we can immediately construct the rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=3-\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -10 \\ 17 & -10\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 3-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13+\text{i} & -10 \\ 17 & -13+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}=0 \\ 17{x}_{1}+(-13+\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix $A-\lambda I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ \frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in C.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

Since we are given the eigenvalue $\lambda =3-\text{i},$ we can immediately construct the rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=3-\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -10 \\ 17 & -10\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 3-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13+\text{i} & -10 \\ 17 & -13+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}=0 \\ 17{x}_{1}+(-13+\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix $A-\lambda I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ \frac{1}{10}(13+\text{i}){x}_{1}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=10$, we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 13+\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we can construct the matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 13 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
